invariants: One native helper measures NSScrollView/NSClipView geometry for existing ordinary text and list controls. It calls native constrainScrollPoint and native view-coordinate conversion, rather than reproducing scrollbar dimensions or clamping/layout algorithms.

Optional control_scroll_geometry appends one pointer at offset 568, preserving the complete previous provider prefix. API remains version 1 with size 576. NXSScrollGeometry aliases the existing text geometry layout; original text methods and capability values remain unchanged.

The size-checked loader exposes generic scroll capability separately from existing list capability. Actual previous 568-byte providers report unsupported and do not change the output buffer; existing list creation/model/pixels remain usable.

Owned generic operation 52 uses NXSControlRequest for kinds 9/13 and returns the native geometry. Bootstrap part 3.y advertises this independently of unchanged part 3.x list capabilities. Creating-connection checks apply; geometry reads remain valid during native tracking.

Shared ListBinding stores native geometry and probes support per host epoch. Its scroll and wheel methods perform existing native RPC and refresh complete snapshots/images; no selection, wheel, coordinate geometry or clamp algorithm is added.

Independent ordinary NSBrowser controls supply geometry and complete real-seat image references at actual 1x/2x, including empty/scrollable/disabled states. A C-only client compares those geometry files through IPC and exercises shared cache methods. A prior compiled list client runs unchanged against the new loader/provider.

Both pinned browser adapters rebuild only to consume the changed shared cache and pass list and text regression images. Original browser, AppKit/backend and 20 measured production hashes remain unchanged. Browser option/layout, DOM scroll and wheel/default routing are not completed by these measurements.
Toolbar/address bar/tabs remain original. Future requested UI changes use optional app-specific patches over the shared layer for browsers and subsequent GTK/Qt/KDE.
